title: UbuntuGuard USB event, version 1
description: A single USB decision event. PRIVACY BOUNDARY: this schema is the enforcement point for 'metadata only'. additionalProperties is false at every level, so a document carrying filename, path, content, bytes_copied or similar is rejected by both the agent and the server. We record which device was seen and what we decided, never what was on it.

event_id.description: Generated by the agent (UUIDv7, so it also sorts by time). The server deduplicates on this value, which is what turns at-least-once delivery into exactly-once storage.

occurred_at.description: Agent wall-clock time of the event. The server also records its own receipt time and flags a delta beyond 300 s rather than rewriting the agent value.

monotonic_ms.description: Agent monotonic clock reading. Lets the server order events correctly even across a wall-clock jump or a suspend/resume cycle.

product_name.description: USB product string as reported by the device. Not trustworthy: any device can claim any name.

serial.description: Null when the device reports no serial, which is common on cheap sticks and is why serial_match='any' exists.

interface_classes.description: Raw USB class:subclass:protocol triples exactly as usbguard reports them. May be EMPTY for a device that was blocked before its interfaces were enumerated, which is precisely why the event source is usbguard's D-Bus signal rather than udev.

connect_type.description: usbguard's with-connect-type. 'hardwired' marks internal devices such as a built-in camera.

parent_hash.description: usbguard parent-hash, used to tell a device behind a hub from the hub itself.

decision.description: 'observed' is what monitor_only produces: we saw it and changed nothing. Reporting it as 'allowed' would overstate what the product did.

decision_source.description: Why the decision happened. 'unknown' is used when the decision was made by usbguard before our policy was loaded, e.g. at boot.

policy.description: Which policy version produced the decision, so an event can be explained months later.
